overall_summary: Family emotional bonds, universal life lessons, and warm connections (Maa, Papa, Bhai, calling loved ones) drastically outperform niche digital heartbreak/self-respect content in views and engagement, though 'self-respect' performs steadily among romantic topics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos about parents, siblings, and calling loved ones (e.g., 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना', Papa/Maa videos) achieved 100 to 286 views, compared to 1-30 views for deep romantic heartbreak shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot more core focus toward universal human relationships and emotional well-being rather than heavily saturated digital-age heartbreak clichés.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos referencing real, tangible human moments (like checking if someone ate or noticing a parent's fatigue) garner immediate engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Keep hooks grounded in recognizable micro-moments of everyday life.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated use of digital-only break-up mechanics like unfollowing, removing widgets, or clearing storage (e.g., 'जब फोन के वॉलपेपर से उसकी पसंद की तस्वीर हटाई', views: 1) resulted in very low traction.
weak_patterns.action: Reduce hyper-specific phone-screen deletion tropes and broaden the emotional resonance.
